items.title: Russia, Ukraine and European security
items.actors:
- **Russia**: [[p:Vladimir Putin]]; Kremlin spokesman [[p:Dmitry Peskov]]; chief of the general staff [[p:Valery Gerasimov]].
- **Ukraine**: President [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] and the Ukrainian armed forces.
- **United States**: President [[p:Donald Trump]] and envoy [[p:Steve Witkoff]], who broker the talks.
- **European states and [[p:NATO]]**: they arm and finance Ukraine and want a seat in the talks.
- **Belarus**: [[p:Alexander Lukashenko]], Moscow's closest ally and a staging ground in 2022.
- **Moldova** (with breakaway Transnistria) and the **Baltic states**: the front-line states.
items.timeline:
- **1991**: The Soviet Union dissolves and Ukraine becomes independent.
- **2014**: The [[e:Revolution of Dignity]] topples Yanukovych. Russia annexes Crimea, and a Russian-backed war starts in Donbas.
- **2015**: The [[e:Minsk agreements]] freeze but do not end the Donbas war.
- **Feb 2022**: Russia launches the [[e:Russian invasion of Ukraine|full-scale invasion]]. Kyiv holds, and Russia retreats from the north.
- **2022–2023**: Ukrainian counter-offensives retake Kharkiv oblast and Kherson city. The 2023 offensive stalls.
- **2024–2026**: A war of attrition in Donetsk oblast, with mass drone and missile strikes on both sides. Finland and Sweden join NATO.
- **2025–2026**: US-brokered [[e:Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|peace talks]] start and stall. Talks revive in October 2026.
items.disputes:
- **Territory**: Russia demands all of Donbas and recognition of its annexations. Kyiv refuses to cede land it holds.
- **Security guarantees**: whether Ukraine gets Western guarantees, foreign troops or a NATO path.
- **Sanctions**: their scope, and how US and EU policy diverge.
- **Frozen Russian assets** and Ukraine's long-term funding.
- **Europe's role**: whether Europeans sit at the table or a US–Russia deal is made over their heads.
items.current:
Diplomacy resumes on 10–11 Nov in Abu Dhabi, where US mediators host working-level talks between a Russian team under [[p:Vladimir Medinsky]] and a Ukrainian one under [[p:Rustem Umerov]]. Kyiv's agenda is an energy truce, Black Sea safety, prisoner exchanges and security guarantees; both sides play down hopes of a breakthrough. [[p:Donald Trump]] talks of a wider deal that "might involve all of Europe", which the EU rejects. The six-day Oleshky ceasefire ended on 1 Nov without extension after about 800 evacuations.

The front is close to static. [[p:Institute for the Study of War|ISW]] estimates Russia lost a little ground in October for a second month, while pressing at Dobropillia and Kostiantynivka. The air war is intensifying: Russia's 3 Nov strike was its largest on Ukraine's energy grid this year and cut Kyiv's water for over a day, and a 2 Nov bombing in Komyshuvakha killed 55. Ukraine hits Russian refineries almost nightly. In Kyiv, the 'Operation Carthage' graft probe reaches into the SBU, and martial law runs to 29 Jan 2027.

In Russia, the 2027 budget raises defence spending by about a third and taxes, and [[p:Novaya Gazeta]] has shut down. On NATO's flank, the US posture review (decision expected in early December) worries Romania and the Baltics, Poland reinforced the Kaliningrad border, and sabotage suspects are being arrested across Europe. Moldova linked its grid to Romania and banned Transnistria's leader from leaving the country. ([Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/umerov-to-lead-ukraine-delegation-in-abu-dhabi-peace-talks-despite-media-confusion-top-official-confirms/), [ISW](https://www.criticalthreats.org/analysis/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-november-1-2026), [Romania Insider](https://romania-insider.com/society/romania-reportedly-willing-help-cover-costs-us-troops))

items.title: The Middle East
items.actors:
- **Israel**: PM [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]] and the IDF.
- **Palestinians**: [[p:Hamas]] in Gaza, and the [[p:Palestinian Authority]] in the West Bank.
- **Iran**: the government and the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]], with allied groups such as [[p:Hezbollah]] in Lebanon and the [[p:Houthis]] in Yemen.
- **United States**: at war with Iran since February 2026.
- **Gulf states**: Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar. Turkey, Egypt, Jordan and Pakistan act as mediators.
items.timeline:
- **1948**: Israel is founded. The 1967 war brings the West Bank and Gaza under Israeli control.
- **1979**: The Iranian revolution makes Iran the region's main anti-US and anti-Israel power.
- **2011**: The Arab uprisings, followed by civil wars in Syria, Yemen and Libya.
- **2015**: The [[e:Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|Iran nuclear deal]]. The US leaves it in 2018.
- **2020**: Under the [[e:Abraham Accords]], Israel normalises ties with the UAE, Bahrain and others.
- **7 Oct 2023**: The Hamas attack on Israel starts the [[e:Gaza war]]. It spreads to Lebanon, the Red Sea and direct Israel–Iran exchanges.
- **Jun 2025**: The [[e:Twelve-Day War]]. Israel and the US strike Iran's nuclear sites.
- **Feb 2026**: US–Israeli strikes start the [[e:2026 Iran war]]. A June interim deal collapses in July, and Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz to "non-compliant" shipping.
items.disputes:
- **Iran**: its nuclear programme and enriched uranium stockpile, and IAEA access.
- **Shipping**: control of the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea lanes.
- **Palestinians**: statehood, and the future of Gaza and the West Bank, including settlements.
- **Lebanon**: Hezbollah's arms and Israel's presence in the south.
- **Saudi–Houthi war**: the Saudi–Houthi conflict in Yemen and its spread to Saudi cities.
items.current:
The [[e:2026 Iran war]] remains in an armed pause. The US keeps up its [[e:naval blockade|2026 United States naval blockade of Iran]], has carried out several "limited" strikes on Qeshm Island since 2 Nov, and disabled a blockade runner on 7 Nov; Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed to most shipping. After the Republicans' midterm losses, diplomacy has picked up: Qatar and Pakistan mediate, Tehran offers to reopen Hormuz within two days if the US ends the war on all fronts, lifts sanctions and the blockade, and [[p:Donald Trump]] met Qatar's prime minister on 9 Nov, citing "positive momentum", while [[p:Marco Rubio]] calls Iran's demands unrealistic. Brent has fallen to about $92. Washington is also pressing Iraq to close most crossings with Iran.

The Saudi–[[p:Houthis|Houthi]] war is drawing in the region: Houthi missiles keep reaching Riyadh and oil sites, Turkey completed ratification of the [[e:Mecca defence pact|Mecca Joint Defence Agreement]] on 4 Nov, Syria signed a defence deal with Riyadh, and AFP sources report Syrian troops deploying to the Saudi–Yemeni border, which Damascus has not confirmed.

In Israel, the 27 Oct election left Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats and [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]]'s at 48; Eisenkot holds the first mandate to form a government and the new Knesset is sworn in on 10 Nov. The Gaza ceasefire remains violent and aid-starved as winter storms flood tent camps, settler violence in the West Bank hit a record in October, and Israeli strikes continue in south Lebanon. ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9/qatar-pm-to-meet-trump-whats-the-latest-on-us-iran-negotiations), [Al-Monitor](https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/11/turkeys-parliament-ratifies-mecca-pact-boost-saudi-arabia), [AFP via Al-Monitor](https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/11/thousands-syrian-troops-deploy-yemen-saudi-arabia-sources-afp), [ynet](https://www.ynet.co.il/news/article/bj5o4ojagx))

items.title: East and Southeast Asia
items.actors:
- **China**: [[p:Xi Jinping]] and the [[p:Chinese Communist Party]], the PLA and the China Coast Guard.
- **Taiwan**: President [[p:Lai Ching-te]].
- **North Korea**: [[p:Kim Jong Un]].
- **South Korea**, and **Japan** under PM [[p:Sanae Takaichi]].
- **United States**: its alliances with Japan, South Korea and the Philippines.
- **[[p:ASEAN]]**: Myanmar's military-led state, and the [[p:Arakan Army]] and other resistance forces.
items.timeline:
- **1949**: The Communist victory in China's civil war. The Nationalists retreat to Taiwan.
- **1950–1953**: The [[e:Korean War]] ends in an armistice, not a peace treaty.
- **1978**: Deng's reforms begin China's rise. Its WTO entry follows in 2001.
- **2006**: North Korea's first nuclear test. Its arsenal grows despite sanctions.
- **2016**: An arbitral tribunal rejects China's sweeping South China Sea claims. Beijing ignores the ruling.
- **2021**: The [[e:2021 Myanmar coup d'état|Myanmar coup]] starts a nationwide civil war.
- **2022–2025**: Large PLA drills around Taiwan, Philippine–Chinese clashes at Second Thomas Shoal, and the US–China tariff war.
- **2026**: APEC is hosted by China (Shenzhen, November), with a possible Trump–Xi–Putin meeting.
items.disputes:
- **Taiwan**: its status, and PLA pressure on the island.
- **South China Sea**: sovereignty over its reefs, especially Second Thomas Shoal and Scarborough Shoal.
- **Korea**: North Korea's nuclear and missile programmes, and the inter-Korean border (the 2026 DMZ landmine row).
- **US–China**: tariffs and technology controls.
- **Myanmar**: its civil war, and the junta's return to ASEAN.
items.current:
Diplomacy is building toward the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov, where the Kremlin says a Putin–Trump–Xi meeting is being prepared. On 24 Oct [[p:Kim Jong Un]] made a one-day trip to Dandong in China, hosted by [[p:Wang Huning]]. Seoul is taking the 21 Sep DMZ landmine blasts to the UN Security Council. Pyongyang denies planting the mines.

In Japan, PM [[p:Sanae Takaichi]]'s approval has slipped after a ministerial resignation. Philippine–Chinese incidents in the South China Sea have increased since 1 Oct, and the two sides dispute whether Manila needed Beijing's "permission" for a 21 Oct resupply mission. Myanmar's junta-backed government seeks a full return to ASEAN while fighting nears Sittwe. Taiwan expects the PLA's late-year drill season, and holds local elections on 28 Nov. ([USNI News](https://news.usni.org/2026/10/09/philippine-and-chinese-incidents-spike-in-south-china-sea-luzon-strait), [NK News](https://www.nknews.org/2026/10/kim-jong-un-says-north-korea-inspired-by-chinas-success-in-border-city-visit/))

items.title: The Americas
items.actors:
- **United States**: President [[p:Donald Trump]] and Secretary of State [[p:Marco Rubio]].
- **Brazil**: [[p:Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] and [[p:Flávio Bolsonaro]].
- **Venezuela**: the interim government of [[p:Delcy Rodríguez]], and the opposition led by [[p:María Corina Machado]].
- **Cuba**: [[p:Miguel Díaz-Canel]].
- **Mexico**: [[p:Claudia Sheinbaum]]. Canada, Colombia, Argentina ([[p:Javier Milei]]) and Peru.
items.timeline:
- **1823**: The Monroe Doctrine.
- **1959**: The Cuban revolution is followed by a US embargo from 1962.
- **1994**: NAFTA, replaced by the USMCA in 2020.
- **1999–2013**: Chávez's "Bolivarian" Venezuela. The Maduro era brings collapse and mass emigration.
- **2025**: Trump's second term brings sweeping tariffs and military strikes on alleged drug boats.
- **Jan 2026**: US forces capture [[p:Nicolás Maduro]]. An energy blockade of Cuba follows.
- **2026**: A rightward electoral swing (Colombia, Peru). Brazil's runoff is on 25 October and the US midterms on 3 November.
items.disputes:
- **Trade**: US tariffs on Canada and Mexico, and the USMCA review.
- **Venezuela**: its transition and an election date.
- **Cuba**: US pressure, and calls for regime change.
- **Migration and drug cartels**: US unilateral force against them.
- **Brazil**: its political polarisation and relations with the US.
items.current:
Democrats swept the 3 Nov [[e:2026 United States elections|midterm elections]], winning the House and at least 54 Senate seats. From January 2027 [[p:Donald Trump]] faces a Congress that has promised to try to end the war with Iran, roll back tariffs and open investigations. Trump says he has no immediate plans to strike Iran, but analysts flag the weeks before the new Congress as risky.

Trade talks have picked up: [[p:Mark Carney]] reports more intense negotiations with Washington, while Mexico failed to land a deal before the vote and still faces Section 232 tariffs. In Venezuela, [[p:Delcy Rodríguez]] promises elections without a date. Washington has met her new foreign minister and reportedly backs a roadmap toward a vote after 2027, and [[p:María Corina Machado]] returned from exile on 25 Oct.

In Brazil, Lula won a fourth term on 25 Oct. Runner-up [[p:Flávio Bolsonaro]] left for Miami via Argentina, prompting a diplomatic row with Buenos Aires. Cuba's blackouts are deepening under the US oil squeeze. In Haiti, El Salvador has sent more than 2,000 troops alongside the [[p:Gang Suppression Force]], and Haiti's elections have slipped to July 2027. ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/senate-election-results-2026/), [Primicias](https://www.primicias.ec/internacional/marco-rubio-reunion-canciller-venezuela-oliver-blanco-136281/), [Al Jazeera](https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/5/el-salvadors-bukele-touts-military-intervention-in-haiti))

items.title: Africa
items.actors:
- **Sudan**: the army under [[p:Abdel Fattah al-Burhan]] against the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]] (RSF).
- **Ethiopia**: PM [[p:Abiy Ahmed]], the [[p:Tigray People's Liberation Front]] and Eritrea.
- **DRC**: the government and the M23-derived rebellion, now led by [[p:Joseph Kabila]]. Rwanda.
- **Sahel juntas** (Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger), the jihadist group [[p:Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal-Muslimin]] and Russia's Africa Corps.
- **The [[p:African Union]]** and Gulf powers (the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar).
items.timeline:
- **1960s**: Decolonisation. The OAU (later the AU) freezes colonial borders.
- **1994**: The Rwandan genocide, followed by the Congo wars of 1996–2003.
- **2011**: South Sudan's independence and the fall of Gaddafi.
- **2012 onwards**: Insurgency in the Sahel. Coups in Mali (2020–21), Burkina Faso (2022) and Niger (2023) bring juntas that turn to Russia.
- **2020–2022**: The [[e:Tigray war]] ends with the Pretoria deal.
- **Apr 2023**: The [[e:Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]] begins. The RSF takes El Fasher in October 2025.
- **2026**: The Ethiopia–Tigray war resumes (September), a large Ebola (Bundibugyo) epidemic hits DRC, and Mali's army retakes Kidal.
items.disputes:
- **Sudan**: power, and Gulf backing for the warring sides.
- **Ethiopia**: Tigray's status, and Ethiopia's quest for sea access versus Eritrea.
- **Eastern DRC**: minerals and Rwanda's role there.
- **The Sahel**: jihadist expansion and the shift from France to Russia.
- **Western Sahara**: its status. The UN's MINURSO mission lapsed in October 2026 after a Russian veto.
items.current:
Overlapping wars, an Ebola epidemic and the end of the UN's Western Sahara mission define the continent.

- **Sudan**: The war between the army and the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]] is centred on Kordofan (around El Obeid), Darfur and Blue Nile. Drone strikes are hitting power stations, fuel depots and aid convoys. Khartoum accuses Ethiopia of letting the RSF launch drones from its soil, and in early November the two expelled each other's diplomats.
- **Ethiopia**: Federal forces took Mekelle in October, but fighting with TPLF-led forces continues in central Tigray and near the Eritrean border. The army has imposed a curfew and a disarmament drive in Mekelle, and Ethiopia–Eritrea tensions remain high.
- **Ebola**: The Bundibugyo epidemic has passed 10,400 confirmed cases in DRC and 5,300 deaths, with cases in Kenya and Nigeria. Vaccine trials are starting.
- **Eastern DRC**: The rebellion led by [[p:Joseph Kabila]] (the FRN) is pressing on Uvira.
- **Western Sahara**: The [[p:United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara|MINURSO]] mandate lapsed on 31 Oct after Russia vetoed a US text backing Morocco's autonomy plan. Rabat says the ceasefire holds, while the [[p:Polisario Front]] warns of war.
- **South Africa**: The 4 Nov local elections are testing the ANC-led coalition, with official results due on 8 Nov.

([Morocco World News](https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2026/11/344641/western-sahara-un-begins-minurso-liquidation/), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/who-approves-trials-for-two-new-ebola-vaccines), [UN News](https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/11/1168731), [Wazema](https://wazema.substack.com/p/ethiopian-army-imposes-nighttime))

items.title: South and Central Asia
items.actors:
- **India**: PM [[p:Narendra Modi]].
- **Pakistan**: the army under [[p:Asim Munir]] and the civilian government. Imran Khan's [[p:Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf]] (PTI).
- **Afghanistan**: the [[p:Taliban]] government. The [[p:Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan]] (TTP).
- **Bangladesh** and **Nepal**: new post-uprising governments.
- **Central Asia**: the five states, with Russia, China and the US competing for influence.
- **The Caucasus**: Armenia (Pashinyan), Azerbaijan (Aliyev), and Georgia, ruled by [[p:Georgian Dream]].
items.timeline:
- **1947**: Partition creates India and Pakistan. Their wars over Kashmir follow in 1947, 1965 and 1999.
- **1991**: The Soviet collapse gives the Central Asian and Caucasus states independence.
- **2001–2021**: The US-led war in Afghanistan ends with the Taliban's return.
- **2020–2023**: Azerbaijan retakes Nagorno-Karabakh.
- **May 2025**: The [[e:2025 India–Pakistan conflict|India–Pakistan conflict]] after the Pahalgam attack.
- **2024–2025**: Uprisings topple governments in Bangladesh (2024) and Nepal (2025).
- **2026**: A Pakistan–Taliban war, Bangladesh's elected government under Tarique Rahman, and an Armenia–Azerbaijan peace process.
items.disputes:
- **India and Pakistan**: Kashmir and the Indus waters.
- **Pakistan and Afghanistan**: the Durand Line and the TTP's sanctuaries.
- **Armenia and Azerbaijan**: the peace treaty and transit routes.
- **Georgia**: its democratic backsliding.
- **Central Asia**: competition between Russia, China and the US over energy and minerals.
items.current:
The war between Pakistan and the Afghan [[p:Taliban]], which began with Pakistani airstrikes in February 2026, continues. There were border clashes into mid-October, and Moscow-format talks ended on 5 Oct without agreement. Islamabad says 1,327 Pakistanis have been killed this year in attacks launched from Afghan soil, and Kabul denies any role. On 11 Oct President Zardari imposed emergency rule in PTI-governed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

India–Pakistan relations remain hostile, with disputes over Kashmir, the Indus waters and a Pakistani airspace ban. Bangladesh's PM Tarique Rahman is courting Japanese investment. Nepal is recovering from deadly August floods. In the Caucasus, Armenia's Pashinyan seeks a peace treaty with Azerbaijan, and Georgia's Constitutional Court is weighing a ban on five opposition parties. ([Long War Journal](https://www.longwarjournal.org/archives/2026/10/taliban-pakistan-border-clashes-continue-after-moscow-talks-end-without-agreement.php), [RFE/RL](https://www.rferl.org/a/georgia-faces-new-test-as-court-weighs-ban-on-five-opposition-parties/33880171.html))

items.title: EU politics and cross-cutting issues
items.actors:
- **EU leaders**: Commission President [[p:Ursula von der Leyen]], European Council President [[p:António Costa]] and foreign-policy chief [[p:Kaja Kallas]].
- **The [[p:European Parliament]]** and the [[p:European Central Bank]] under [[p:Christine Lagarde]].
- **Member state leaders**: Germany ([[p:Friedrich Merz]]), France (Macron, with PM [[p:Sébastien Lecornu]]), Poland ([[p:Donald Tusk]]), Italy ([[p:Giorgia Meloni]]) and Hungary ([[p:Péter Magyar]]).
- **Global bodies**: the [[p:United Nations Security Council]], the [[p:International Atomic Energy Agency]] and [[p:OPEC]].
items.timeline:
- **1957**: The Treaty of Rome. The 1992 Maastricht Treaty creates the EU and the path to the euro.
- **2004–2013**: Eastern enlargement, from 15 members to 28.
- **2010–2012**: The eurozone debt crisis.
- **2015**: The migration crisis.
- **2016–2020**: [[e:Brexit]].
- **2022**: Russia's invasion leads to the EU's sanctions packages, a break with Russian gas, and candidate status for Ukraine and Moldova.
- **2026**: Hungary's change of government (Magyar), Ukraine's accession clusters opening, an energy shock from the Iran war, and talks on the 2028–34 budget.
items.disputes:
- **Enlargement**: its pace (Ukraine, Moldova, the Western Balkans), and vetoes.
- **The budget**: the 2028–34 long-term budget, and financing Ukraine.
- **Energy**: security and the Russian LNG phase-out.
- **Rule of law and populism** in member states.
- **Relations with the US**: transatlantic trade and security ties.
- **Arms control**: nuclear arms control after New START.
- **UN**: the paralysis of the Security Council and the 2026 Secretary-General selection.
items.current:
Europe is under pressure on three fronts.

- **Energy**: The [[e:2026 Iran war]] has cost the EU an extra €127 billion for oil and gas, says [[p:Ursula von der Leyen]]. Gas storage is about 74%, some 12 points below normal, as winter begins.
- **Washington and Moscow**: [[p:Donald Trump]] hints at a deal with Russia that "might involve all of Europe". [[p:Kaja Kallas]] says Moscow has no veto over European security. Beijing confirms talks on a Xi–Trump–Putin meeting at APEC.
- **Domestic strain**: France's 2027 budget fell in the Assembly, and strikes drew 575,000 people on 5 Nov (Interior Ministry count). Poland is locked in a fight over its [[p:Constitutional Tribunal (Poland)|Constitutional Tribunal]]. Sweden still has no government, and Spain votes on 29 Nov.

The [[e:2026 Serbian parliamentary election]] ended [[p:Aleksandar Vučić]]'s dominance: the [[p:Student List]] won 140 of 250 seats. The 4 Nov enlargement package set roadmaps for Montenegro, Albania, Moldova and Ukraine. Hungary is still holding Ukraine's clusters 4 and 5. [[p:Christine Lagarde]] leaves the ECB in February, and the EU budget for 2028–34 is due by December. ([European Commission](https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/news/2026-enlargement-package-shows-reform-commitment-delivers-progress-towards-eu-membership-2026-11-04_en), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/06/eu-rejects-trumps-big-beautiful-security-deal-with-russia-and-all-of-europe))
